stem: Where must evaluation numbers come from?
options: Rows the model never trained on

stem: With 30% positives, 'always predict no' has 70% accuracy. What follows?
options: Positives are too rare to model
Accuracy misleads with imbalance; use recall/precision on the rare class and beat this baseline
explanation: Every model must beat a baseline on a metric that reflects the goal.

stem: Reviewers complain about false alarms. Honest offer?
options: Raise the threshold: fewer FP, more FN — decide the line together
explanation: At a fixed model the threshold trades precision for recall.

options: Ranking quality — P(random positive outranks random negative), threshold-free
explanation: Compare models on AUC; choose thresholds afterwards.

stem: 0.94 AUC on a random split of 3 years of data; production is much worse. Likely?
options: Random split let the model train on the future — split by time
explanation: Evaluate the way production experiences it: past → future.

stem: A feature 'refund_issued' when predicting fraud is…
options: Leakage — not known at prediction time
explanation: Ask 'would we know this at prediction time?' for every feature.

stem: Why look at metrics per segment?
options: Averages hide the group the model fails for; this is where bias shows
explanation: Slices and a read sample, not one number.

options: The same discipline: held-out set, confusion matrix, precision/recall, slices, a read sample
